To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
renal responses to reflex activation of renal nerves were similar in normo- and hypertensive animals.
renal sympathetic nerve activation is not enhanced in hypertension associated with activation and suppression of the renin angiotensin system.
renal hemodynamic and excretory function is relatively normal in angio-tensin-dependent hypertension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural regulation of renal function in hypertension.
the role of renal nerves and renal denervation on renal hemodynamics and renal function.
the role of the renal nerves in the pathogenesis of hypertension and the mechanisms by which they exert their effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kidney is relatively normal in its responsiveness to neural activation in ANG II-dependent hypertension.
the renal responses to acute reflex increases in RSAA are relatively normal in ANG II-dependent hypertension.
renal denervation does not alter renal hemodynamic or excretory functions but reduces renal PRA overflow in the hypertensive animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in angiotensinsensitive hypertension, the responsiveness of the renal vasculature and tubule is normal and that the reduced responsiveness of the renin system to increases in RSNA is due to reduced neural norepiinephrine release and enhanced postjunctional reactivities.
the renal sympathetic nervous system is not involved in the pathogenesis of angiotensin-induced hypertension.
the kidney is not a key player in the development of hypertension in rabbits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neural control of renal blood flow and excretory function is relatively normal in angotensin-dependent hypertension.
the renal sympathetic nervous system does not contribute to hypertension in this model of ANG II-mediated hypertension.
renal sympathetic nerve activity does not play a significant role in the pathophysiology of hypertension associated with the activation of the rennin-angiotensine system.
